title: Open Source AI Salons and What’s Next
content:
Dear OSI community,

The fall conference season in the US is especially busy. I’ve been fortunate enough to attend several events in the last month, but it was especially great to reconnect with the community at All Things Open. This was my first big Open Source conference as Executive Director as we hosted the State of the Source track. Many of our sessions were standing room only, and the feedback we heard was generous and useful. We’re grateful for that, and we’ll be posting recordings of the sessions soon.

The day after All Things Open, we hosted our first Open Source AI Salon. This was an important moment for us as we re-engage the community to discuss the Open Source AI Definition, look at everything we’ve collectively learned since version 1.0 was published two years ago, and chart the course for our next steps. We’ll be hosting many more of these events in the coming months. Watch this space for details.

title: Open Source AI Salons: Shaping the OSAID, Together
content:
Two years after the release of the Open Source AI Definition (OSAID 1.0), the Open Source Initiative hosted the first in a series of Open Source AI Salons, gatherings to discuss the future of the OSAID. In collaboration with key partners in Raleigh and Barcelona, the events brought together civil society, government, industry, and academia to understand the practical application of the OSAID.

These interdisciplinary, community-driven events provide the ground to surface challenges, examine assumptions, and explore practical issues affecting the Open Source community when it comes to AI. As we head into 2027, we are developing opportunities to bring candid discussions about the OSAID to more people in more places. OSI is steadfast in its commitment to empowering the Open Source community and promoting a healthy Open Source AI ecosystem.
